title: Isolation and Characterization of Small Extracellular Vesicles from Human Menstrual Fluid
author: Tang, Zhou, et al.
materials:
This step describes the removal of cells, platelets, and large debris from menstrual fluid to obtain a clarified, cell-free menstrual serum suitable for small extracellular vesicle isolation.6.Upon arrival at the laboratory, dilute the menstrual fluid with an equal volume of particle-free DPBS. Gently mix by inversion to avoid bubble formation.Note: Depending on downstream applications, users may consider including protease inhibitors during early processing steps to minimize protein degradation.7.Pre-wet a 100
μm cell strainer (Falcon, Corning, #352360) with particle-free DPBS, pass the diluted sample through into a new 50 mL conical tube.8.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C to remove intact cells and big debris. Carefully collect the supernatant without disturbing the pellets.9.Centrifuge the filtrate at 2,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.a.Transfer the clarified supernatant to a new sterile 50 mL Falcon tube.10.Pass the supernatant through a 0.22
μm syringe filter (Merck Millipore Ltd., Cat# SLGP033RS) to obtain sterile cell-free menstrual serum.Note: The 0.22 μm filtration step is included to remove residual debris and aggregates that may interfere with downstream size-exclusion chromatography performance. However, filtration may also result in partial loss of vesicles due to membrane retention or clogging, particularly for viscous samples. Users may consider evaluating particle recovery (e.g. by NTA before and after filtration) and adjusting the filtration strategy depending on sample characteristics and whether purity or yield is prioritized.11.Dispense the filtered serum into 500
μL aliquots using sterile low binding tubes (Axygen, MCT-150-L-C). Proceed to sEV isolation immediately or store the aliquots at −80°C until use for EV isolation. Avoid repeated freeze–thaw cycles.Note: The menstrual blood serum can be stored at −80°C for up to half a year prior to EV isolation without significant loss of EV integrity. Samples should be thawed on ice before use.
Timing: Approximately 5 min per sample for acquisition

steps.title: Dilute menstrual fluid
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of particle‑free DPBS to the received menstrual fluid and gently mix by inversion to avoid bubble formation.

steps.title: Pre‑wet cell strainer
steps.instruction: Pre‑wet a 100 µm cell strainer (Falcon, Corning, #352360) with particle‑free DPBS, then pass the diluted sample through the strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Remove cells and large debris
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtrate at 400 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Carefully collect the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Further clarification
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collected supernatant at 2,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C, then transfer the clarified supernatant to a new sterile 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: 0.22 µm filtration
steps.instruction: Pass the supernatant through a 0.22 µm syringe filter (Merck Millipore, Cat# SLGP033RS) to obtain sterile, cell‑free menstrual serum.

steps.title: Aliquot serum
steps.instruction: Dispense the filtered serum into 500 µL aliquots using sterile low‑binding tubes (Axygen, MCT‑150‑L‑C). Use immediately for sEV isolation or store at –80 °C (up to 6 months) on ice‑thaw; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Assemble qEV rack
steps.instruction: Place the base platform on a level bench, insert the two vertical support arms, attach the top plate by aligning side slots and pressing down until locked, then verify the rack is stable and upright before inserting the column.

steps.title: Insert and equilibrate column
steps.instruction: Insert the qEVoriginal 70 nm (Gen 2) column vertically into the rack with the narrow luer outlet facing downward. Keep caps on and allow the column and sample buffer to equilibrate at 18 °C–24 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Flush column with DPBS
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom luer cap to start gravity flow, let the storage buffer run, then flush the column with at least 17 mL particle‑free DPBS to the top reservoir, collecting the effluent in waste. If the column will not be used immediately, replace the bottom cap and keep the resin bed covered with DPBS to prevent drying.

steps.title: Warm up NTA instrument
steps.instruction: Turn on the ZetaView NTA (PMX‑230‑7, Germany) and allow it to warm up for 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare NTA software
steps.instruction: Turn on the computer, open ZetaNavigator software, and wait until all indicators turn green.

steps.title: Rinse NTA flow cell
steps.instruction: Click “Rinse” and run water through the flow cell for 30 seconds. If air bubbles appear, pump once more; repeat a second rinse if fresh water was added.

steps.title: Load size standard
steps.instruction: Prepare polystyrene size standard at a 1/250 000 dilution, inject it with a 1 mL syringe avoiding air bubbles, then click “Autofocus”. Accept a yellow range; autofocus values 0–8 are acceptable.

steps.title: Dilute and load EV sample
steps.instruction: Dilute each EV sample with particle‑free DPBS to a total volume of 1 mL, inject the 1 mL into the NTA (avoid bubbles) and ensure the particle count is between 10 and 100 per screen.

steps.title: Acquire NTA data
steps.instruction: Analyze the sample at 11 positions using ZetaNavigator with settings: laser 488 nm, sensitivity 82, shutter 100, sequence length 30, frame rate 30, temperature 25 °C.

steps.title: Clean between samples
steps.instruction: Rinse the flow cell with particle‑free DPBS until the particle count drops below 10 per screen before loading the next sample.

steps.title: Final instrument cleaning
steps.instruction: Flush the flow cell with 20 mL particle‑free deionized water repeatedly until the particle count is below 10 per screen.
